CPD

Here is how to approximate a tensor A by a CPD of rank r.

julia> using TensorKitchen
julia> A = randn(20, 15, 10)
julia> r = 35
julia> res = cpd(A, r)
CPDResult{Float64}
  Order:        3
  Dimensions:   (20, 15, 10)
  Rank:         35
  Rel. error:   0.4359141301703327

Now, res contains a CP approximation of the 3-way tensor A,

\[\hat A = \sum_{i=1}^r \lambda_i\, a_i \otimes b_i \otimes c_i\]

It approximates A with relative error about 0.436.

We access the decomposition as follows.

λ = weights(res)
U = factors(res)

Here, U is a triple of matrices $(A,B,C)$, where the columns of $A$ are the $a_i$ and so on. These are called factor matrices.

We get the whole reconstructed tensor by 

Â = reconstruct(res)

TensorKitchen.cpd — Function
cpd(A, r, opts::CPDOpts)
cpd(A, r; kwargs...)

Rank-r CP decomposition of A; :als converges linearly with rate ≈ 0.83 (~200 iters to machine precision on exact low-rank CP).

source
TensorKitchen.nncpd — Function
nncpd(A; r=nothing, kwargs...) -> CPDResult

Nonnegative CP decomposition. If r is omitted, uses the same rank heuristic as cpd(A; r=nothing, ...).

source
nncpd(A, r; kwargs...) -> CPDResult

Nonnegative CP decomposition with its own frontend defaults.

source
TensorKitchen.CPDResult — Type
CPDResult{T}

Result of a Canonical Polyadic Decomposition.

  • components: vector of RankOneTensor
  • cost, rel_error, grad_norm, iterations, converged, solver: metadata
  • solver_info: lightweight solver diagnostics (for example line-search/evaluation counts)
source
TensorKitchen.RankOneTensor — Type
RankOneTensor{T}

Representation of a rank-one tensor λ · u₁ ⊗ u₂ ⊗ … ⊗ u_d.

  • λ: scalar weight
  • vectors: length-d vector of factor vectors (one per mode)

Not a manifold object; used for CP representation and contractions.

source

weights(r::CPDResult) -> Vector{T}

Return the per-component scalar weights [λ_1, …, λ_r].

source
TensorKitchen.comp_weight — Method
comp_weight(r::CPDResult)

Return component weights from solver_info(r) when available, otherwise fall back to weights.

source
TensorKitchen.factors — Method
factors(r::CPDResult) -> Vector{Matrix{T}}

Return the mode-wise factor matrices (A, B, C, …); column k of mode m is the m-th factor vector of the k-th rank-one component.

source
TensorKitchen.reconstruct — Method
reconstruct(r::CPDResult)

Reconstruct the tensor: ∑k λk · (U1[:,k] ⊗ U2[:,k] ⊗ …).

normalize_components!(point::CPDPoint, policy=SeparateLambdaNormalization())

Normalize a canonical CPDPoint in place.

This is the preferred backend entry point for normalization, since it is independent of solver/manifold layout. To normalize an actual optimization iterate, combine it with cpd_point and pack_cpd_point, or use post_step!.
